context.body: Jesus went out from there and withdrew into the region of Tyre and Sidon.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: The woman cries for mercy and her daughter, meets silence and disciple pressure, debates lost sheep and household crumbs, is commended for faith, and her daughter is healed.
observations.label: A Canaanite woman calls the Son of David: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps Jesus, the Canaanite woman, her daughter, and disciples, the region of Tyre and Sidon and the road, crying “Son of David,” remaining silent, urging dismissal, answering, kneeling, disputing imagery, commending, and healing visible within David's story or later memory.
observations.label: A Canaanite woman calls the Son of David: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: Jesus, the Canaanite woman, her daughter, and disciples · the region of Tyre and Sidon and the road · crying “Son of David,” remaining silent, urging dismissal, answering, kneeling, disputing imagery, commending, and healing · a Davidic plea persists through boundary language until healing is announced
observations.label: Relationships named in Matthew 15:21–28

payload.posture: Read Matthew 15:21–28 as its own gospel and apostolic memory David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places a Davidic plea persists through boundary language until healing is announced inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
